summary: Harborview Health Network needs a HIPAA-compliant clinical-document intake pipeline and a retrieval-grounded patient-support assistant on AWS, integrated with Epic via FHIR R4, serving roughly 1,200 staff and 85,000 monthly patient encounters with a 24-week phased rollout; Epic sandbox write access and the assistant's deployment form remain open.

items.title: Cut document-keying time by 50%
items.description: Reduce the time medical records clerks spend keying referral and prior-authorisation documents into Epic by at least 50%.

source.quote: BR1. The solution must reduce the time medical records clerks spend keying referral and prior-authorisation documents into Epic by at least 50%.

items.title: Reduce routine front-desk call volume
items.description: Reduce routine front-desk call volume by giving patients a self-service way to get appointment-prep and billing answers.

source.quote: BR2. The solution must reduce routine front-desk call volume by giving patients a self-service way to get appointment-prep and billing answers.

items.title: Faster document-to-chart visibility
items.description: Reduce the average time from document receipt to the document being visible in a patient's Epic chart.

source.quote: BR3. The solution should reduce the average time from document receipt to the document being visible in a patient's Epic chart.

items.title: Clinical decisions stay with licensed staff
items.description: Every clinical or coverage decision remains with a licensed staff member; the assistant never makes an autonomous clinical or eligibility determination.

source.quote: BR4. Every clinical or coverage decision must remain with a licensed staff member; the assistant must never make an autonomous clinical or eligibility determination.

items.title: Behavioural-health screening (future candidate)
items.description: Extending to behavioural-health intake screening is a future candidate but explicitly out of scope for this initial phase.

source.quote: BR5. The solution could eventually extend to behavioural-health intake screening, though that is out of scope for this initial phase.

items.title: Multi-channel document intake
items.description: Accept incoming referral letters, prior-authorisation forms and lab results from fax, secure email and patient-portal upload.

source.quote: FR1. The system must accept incoming referral letters, prior-authorisation forms and lab results from fax, secure email and patient-portal upload.

items.title: Structured field extraction
items.description: Extract structured fields from each document, including patient identifiers, referring provider, requested service and supporting clinical notes.

source.quote: FR2. The system must extract structured fields from each document, including patient identifiers, referring provider, requested service and supporting clinical notes.

items.title: Mandatory clerk review before write-back
items.description: Present each extracted document to a medical records clerk for review and correction before anything is written to Epic.

source.quote: FR3. The system must present each extracted document to a medical records clerk for review and correction before anything is written to Epic.

items.title: Approved-document write-back to Epic
items.description: Write approved documents back to the correct patient chart in Epic through the FHIR R4 API, tagged with the extracting user and timestamp.

source.quote: FR4. Approved documents must be written back to the correct patient chart in Epic through the FHIR R4 API, tagged with the extracting user and timestamp.

items.title: Patient-support assistant Q&A
items.description: The patient-support assistant answers common questions about appointment preparation, clinic locations, hours and accepted insurance plans.

source.quote: FR5. The patient-support assistant must answer common questions about appointment preparation, clinic locations, hours and accepted insurance plans.

items.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content
items.description: The assistant retrieves answers from approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.

source.quote: FR6. The patient-support assistant must retrieve answers from our approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.

items.title: Escalation for clinical-judgement questions
items.description: The assistant recognises when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and hands off to a human staff member.

source.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.

items.title: Prioritised clerk review queue
items.description: Medical records clerks see a queue of documents awaiting review, prioritised by how long they have been waiting.

source.quote: FR9. Medical records clerks must be able to see a queue of documents awaiting review, prioritised by how long they have been waiting.

items.title: Assistant availability through the patient portal and public website
items.description: The patient-support assistant is available through the existing patient portal and, where feasible, as a widget on the public website.

source.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.

items.title: Low-confidence extraction flagging for clerk review
items.description: Documents where extraction confidence is low are flagged so medical records clerks review those first.

source.quote: FR10. The system should flag documents where extraction confidence is low so clerks review those first.

items.title: 85,000 patient encounters per month at scale
items.description: Process at least 85,000 patient encounters worth of associated documents per month without a growing backlog.

source.quote: NFR1. The intake system must process at least 85,000 patient encounters worth of associated documents per month without a growing backlog.

items.title: 5-minute extraction turnaround
items.description: Document extraction results must be available to a reviewing clerk within 5 minutes of document receipt for 95% of documents.

source.quote: NFR2. Document extraction results must be available to a reviewing clerk within 5 minutes of document receipt for 95% of documents.

items.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations
items.description: Support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.

source.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.

items.title: 99.5% availability during clinic hours
items.description: Maintain 99.5% availability during clinic operating hours, 7am to 8pm Pacific, seven days a week.

source.quote: NFR5. The system must maintain 99.5% availability during clinic operating hours, 7am to 8pm Pacific, seven days a week.

items.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers
items.description: Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.

source.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.

items.title: 4-second assistant response time
items.description: The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.

source.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.

items.title: Epic FHIR R4 write and read integration
items.description: Integrate with Epic through the FHIR R4 API to write structured document data and retrieve patient context.

source.quote: INT1. The intake system must integrate with Epic through the FHIR R4 API to write structured document data and retrieve patient context.

items.title: Inbound document channel integration
items.description: Accept inbound documents from the existing fax gateway, secure email inbox and patient-portal upload mechanism.

source.quote: INT2. The intake system must accept inbound documents from our existing fax gateway, secure email inbox and patient-portal upload mechanism.

items.title: Five9 handoff integration
items.description: The patient-support assistant integrates with Five9 so a handed-off conversation routes to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.

source.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.

items.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse
items.description: Authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.

source.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.

items.title: CareEverywhere query integration (later phase)
items.description: Querying the regional CareEverywhere health information exchange is desired in a later phase but not required for go-live.

source.quote: INT5. The solution should be able to query the regional CareEverywhere health information exchange in a later phase, but that integration is not required for go-live.

items.title: Protected health information handling
items.description: All patient documents and extracted fields are protected health information and must be handled under HIPAA policies at every stage.

source.quote: DATA1. All patient documents and extracted fields are protected health information and must be handled under our HIPAA policies at every stage.

items.title: Approved-content-only assistant knowledge base
items.description: The assistant's knowledge base is built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.

source.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.

items.title: Six-year document and conversation retention
items.description: Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.

source.quote: DATA3. Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.

items.title: Conversation-log governance for model training
items.description: Conversation logs are reviewable by compliance staff but must not be used to retrain or fine-tune any model without a separate, explicit approval process.

source.quote: DATA4. Conversation logs must be reviewable by compliance staff but must not be used to retrain or fine-tune any model without a separate, explicit approval process.

items.title: Separated encryption for documents and sessions
items.description: Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.

source.quote: DATA5. Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.

items.title: HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA
items.description: Comply with HIPAA, including a signed business associate agreement with any AI provider or subprocessor involved.

source.quote: SEC1. The solution must comply with HIPAA, including a signed business associate agreement with any AI provider or subprocessor involved.

items.title: PHI encryption in transit and at rest
items.description: Encrypt all protected health information in transit and at rest using current industry-standard algorithms.

source.quote: SEC2. All protected health information must be encrypted in transit and at rest using current industry-standard algorithms.

items.title: Role-based review-queue access
items.description: Access to the document-review queue is role-based and limited to authorised medical records staff, with supervisor audit visibility.

source.quote: SEC3. Access to the document-review queue must be role-based and limited to authorised medical records staff, with supervisor audit visibility.

items.title: MFA for review-queue access
items.description: Enforce multi-factor authentication for all staff accessing the intake review queue or extracted patient data.

source.quote: SEC4. Multi-factor authentication must be enforced for all staff accessing the intake review queue or extracted patient data.

items.title: HIPAA security risk assessment before go-live
items.description: Undergo a HIPAA security risk assessment before go-live.

source.quote: SEC5. The solution must undergo a HIPAA security risk assessment before go-live.

items.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute
items.description: The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.

source.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.

items.title: AWS as target cloud platform
items.description: The infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and prefers the new platform to run on AWS.

source.quote: TECH1. Our infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and would prefer the new intake and assistant platform to run on AWS.

items.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant
items.description: Open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it meets HIPAA and data-handling requirements.

source.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.

items.title: Python skill alignment for handover
items.description: The two in-house developers have Python experience and would like to maintain integration code after handover.

source.quote: TECH3. Our two in-house developers have Python experience and would like to be able to maintain integration code after handover.

items.title: 24-week phased rollout starting with intake
items.description: A phased rollout starts with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.

source.quote: CON1. We would like a phased rollout starting with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.

items.title: Compliance sign-off before any patient-facing pilot
items.description: The compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.

source.quote: CON3. Our compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.

items.title: Fallback to today's manual process during rollout
items.description: The medical records team can fall back to today's manual process at any time during the initial rollout if extraction quality is not yet trusted.

source.quote: CON2. The medical records team must be able to fall back to today's manual process at any time during the initial rollout if extraction quality is not trusted yet.

items.title: Limited subject-matter-expert availability during build
items.description: Clinical and administrative staff can provide at most one subject-matter expert two days a week during the build; the delivery partner is expected to own the technical build.

source.quote: CON4. Clinical and administrative staff can provide at most one subject-matter expert two days a week during the build; the delivery partner is expected to own the technical build.

items.title: Epic EHR
items.description: The electronic health record system of record across all six clinics and the referral centre, exposed through Epic's FHIR R4 API.

source.quote: Epic is our electronic health record system of record across all six clinics and the referral centre, exposed to partners through Epic's FHIR R4 API.

items.title: Five9 Contact Centre
items.description: The current cloud contact-centre product front-desk staff use for the 12,000 monthly patient calls.

source.quote: Our current phone system is a cloud contact-centre product from Five9, which front-desk staff use today for the 12,000 monthly patient calls.

items.title: CareEverywhere Health Information Exchange
items.description: A regional health information exchange used ad hoc by physicians to pull outside records, not integrated into the intake workflow today.

source.quote: A regional health information exchange, CareEverywhere, is used ad hoc by physicians to pull outside records, but is not integrated into our intake workflow.

items.title: Manual Document Scanning Process
items.description: Incoming documents are currently scanned into a shared network drive and manually filed by the medical records team before being keyed into Epic.

source.quote: Incoming documents are currently scanned into a shared network drive and manually filed by the medical records team before being keyed into Epic.

items.title: Patient Portal
items.description: The clinic's existing patient-facing portal, used today for patient login and document upload, that the assistant must also be reachable through.

source.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.

items.title: Medical Records Clerk
items.description: One of eleven staff who manually read and key referral and prior-authorisation documents into Epic today, and who will review extracted data.

source.quote: Referral letters, prior-authorisation forms and outside lab results arrive by fax, secure email and patient portal upload, and today a team of eleven medical records clerks manually reads and keys each document into our EHR.

items.title: Patient
items.description: Calls or messages the clinic with appointment-prep, billing and insurance questions and will interact with the support assistant.

source.quote: Our clinics see approximately 85,000 patient encounters per month across primary care, behavioural health and physical therapy.

items.title: Business associate agreement execution
items.description: A signed business associate agreement with the chosen AI provider must be reviewed and executed before any pilot can begin.

source.quote: The Compliance Officer confirmed a business associate agreement will be required with whichever AI provider is ultimately used and asked to review that agreement before any pilot.

items.title: Extraction-accuracy risk across document sources
items.description: Documents arrive by fax, secure email and portal upload with varying quality, creating a risk of inconsistent extraction accuracy across sources.

source.quote: Referral letters, prior-authorisation forms and outside lab results arrive by fax, secure email and patient portal upload, and today a team of eleven medical records clerks manually reads and keys each document into our EHR.

items.title: Spanish-language coverage gap at launch
items.description: About 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but Spanish-language conversations are not committed to for the initial assistant phase, risking uneven adoption.

source.quote: The Director of Patient Access asked whether the assistant could eventually support Spanish-language conversations, given about 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but this was not committed to for the initial phase.

items.title: Epic sandbox write capability unconfirmed
items.description: It is unclear whether the current Epic FHIR R4 sandbox supports writing structured referral data or only reading patient context.

source.quote: It is still unclear whether Epic's FHIR R4 API in our current sandbox environment supports writing structured referral data or only reading patient context; the CMIO will confirm with the Epic team.

items.title: Assistant deployment form undecided
items.description: No decision has been made on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded inside the existing patient portal.

source.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.

items.title: Target phase for the CareEverywhere integration not set
items.description: The customer defers the CareEverywhere health information exchange integration past go-live but has not said which later phase should deliver it.

source.quote: INT5. The solution should be able to query the regional CareEverywhere health information exchange in a later phase, but that integration is not required for go-live.

items.title: AI provider must support a HIPAA BAA
items.description: Assumed the selected AI/ML provider can execute a HIPAA business associate agreement; providers unable to sign a BAA are out of consideration.

source.quote: SEC1. The solution must comply with HIPAA, including a signed business associate agreement with any AI provider or subprocessor involved.

items.title: Policy documents are reusable for a knowledge base
items.description: Assumed the clinic's existing policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents are already in a reusable digital format suitable for a knowledge base.

source.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.

items.title: Does the Epic FHIR R4 sandbox support writing referral data?
items.description: Confirm whether the Epic FHIR R4 sandbox supports writing structured referral data or is currently read-only for patient context.

source.quote: It is still unclear whether Epic's FHIR R4 API in our current sandbox environment supports writing structured referral data or only reading patient context; the CMIO will confirm with the Epic team.

items.title: Should the assistant be standalone or embedded in the portal?
items.description: Confirm whether the patient-support assistant should ship as a standalone application or be embedded in the existing patient portal.

source.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.

items.title: Confirm the target phase for the CareEverywhere integration
items.description: The customer says the CareEverywhere integration is not required for go-live; confirm which later phase should deliver it so it can be planned and estimated then.

source.quote: A regional health information exchange, CareEverywhere, is used ad hoc by physicians to pull outside records, but is not integrated into our intake workflow.
